subStrands.name: Position and Direction
content: Clockwise and an anti- clockwise turn

outcomes.text: identify a clockwise and an anti-clockwise turn in the environment
demonstrate a clockwise and an anti-clockwise turn in the environment
identify quarter, half and full turns direction in the environment
demonstrate a quarter turn, half turn and full turn direction in the environment
appreciate use of position and direction in real-life situations

learningExperiences: make clockwise or anticlockwise turns
discuss and demonstrate a clockwise turn
team up with peers to demonstrate an anti-clockwise turn
work with peers to safely make quarter, half and full turns in the surroundings
team up with peers to demonstrate a quarter turn in both directions
demonstrate a half turn from a point
demonstrate a full turn from a point
jointly with others, play digital games involving position and direction
coreCompetencies: Learning to learn: learner works collaboratively with others while making clockwise or anticlockwise turns in the environment.
values: Unity: learner embraces others as they demonstrate a clockwise turn.
pcis: Safety: learner observes care and precautions while making quarter, half and full turns in the environment.
links: The learner is able to relate making quarter, half and full turns in the surroundings to the location, position and size of Kenya in Social Studies.

subStrands.name: Angles

outcomes.text: identify an angle at a point in lines
identify angles from the objects in the environment
relate a turn to angles in real-life situations
appreciate use of angles in real-life situations

learningExperiences: discuss and recognise angles that are made by 2 lines that meet at point using a chart with a different line
team u[ with peers to explore and identify angles from objects such as cubes and cuboids in the environment
make clockwise quarter and half turns, and relate the turns to angles
play digital games and learn more about angles
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we use angles in daily life?
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: learner collaboratively works with others and recognises angles that are made by 2 lines that meet at a point using a chart with a different line.
values: Responsibility: learner observes safety precautions while identifying angles from objects such as cubes, cuboids in the environment.
pcis: Environmental Education: learner explores and identifies angles from objects such as cubes, and cuboids in the environment.
links: The learner is able to relate angles from objects such as cubes and cuboids in the environment to perspective in Creative Arts.

subStrands.name: Plane Figures
content: Rectangles, squares, triangles, circles and ovals

outcomes.text: identify rectangles, squares, triangles, circles and ovals from objects in the environment
draw the shapes of rectangles, squares, triangles, circles and ovals from objects in the environment
identify lines of symmetry of different shapes
make patterns using squares, rectangles and triangles
identify properties of plane figures in different situations
appreciate using shapes in real-life situations

learningExperiences: discuss and recognise shapes of rectangles, squares, triangles, circles and ovals from common objects in the environment
sketch the shapes of rectangles, squares, triangles, circles and ovals in their books or charts using objects in the environment
discuss and fold the shapes into two equal parts and recognise the fold line as the line of symmetry
discuss how many lines of symmetry can each shape possibly have by folding the shapes
work with peers to make patterns using squares, rectangles and triangles
identify the properties of a square practically
discuss the properties of a rectangle practically
identify properties of a triangle practically
collaboratively use digital devices to learnmore about plane figures and make patterns
keyInquiryQuestions: How can you make patterns using shapes?
coreCompetencies: Creativity and imagination: learner explores new ideas while making patterns using squares, rectangles and triangles.
values: Respect: learner displays humility while recognising shapes of rectangles, squares, triangles, circles and ovals from common objects in the environment.
pcis: Peer Education and Mentorship: learner exhibits teamwork while sketching the shapes of rectangles, squares, triangles, circles and ovals from objects in the environment.
links: The learner is able to relate making patterns using squares, rectangles and triangles to perspective in Creative Arts.

subStrands.name: Data

outcomes.text: identify materials for data collection and recording in real-life situations
collect data of at most 10 items within the school environment
draw a table for recording data
record data in the table
interpret the raw data from the table
appreciate use of tables in representing data in real-life situations

learningExperiences: name and gather different materials that can used for data collection and recording such as rulers, exercise books for drawing tables, and textbooks
collect and record data on different items such the types of vehicles in the environment
team up with peers to represent the raw data in simple tables
explain and interpret the raw data from the table
explain the data on the types of vehicles in relation to responding to emergencies in case they are hurt while on the road
team up with peers to use digital devices or other resources for data collection and recording
coreCompetencies: Critical thinking and problem solving: learner explores new ways of gathering and sharing different items for the purposes of recording data.
values: Patriotism: learner exhibits honesty while gathering and sharing different items for the purposes of recording data.
pcis: Environmental Education: learner collects materials from the immediate classroom environment.
links: The learner is able to relate data collection and recording to Democracy in society in Social Studies.
